hypothesis: The resident OS image with the performance service, eight recognition workers, admitted A76 cores, CPU clock grants, GPU and ShuffleNet model 3 fits its budgets, and the stopped-NPU retune command passes its host and native cases
prediction: Budget: no task, stack, heap allocation or model copy added; the session stays 1,176 bytes with four card extents; the reused monitor stays within its fixed 32 KiB limit; inference and idle ticks incur no new retune work. The stopped NPU command adds an eight-byte deadline mailbox and constant ownership and time checks, and keeps the existing five PLL writes.
conclusion: All budgets met and all cases pass. These native cases model the thermal task's publication and do not claim a completed hardware transition; modeled elapsed time does not establish physical latency. Physical runtime switching, thermal recovery and cold retirement still need the bound evidence. All generated card records are modeled and nondeployable.
narrative:
Size, relative to the accepted fixed-point resident CPU/GPU/NPU image: the complete resident image adds 28,512 allocated CODE bytes and 1,536 BSS bytes. Initialized data remains 1,118,048 bytes, including the NPU payloads in non-executable RAM. CODE has 732,848 bytes free within its existing 2 MiB mapping. The write-back device pool still ends at 0x41b27000, leaving 888,832 bytes before the uncached pool. The reused monitor is 32,456 bytes within its fixed 32 KiB limit. The session remains 1,176 bytes with four card extents (the 904- and 1,176-byte CPU and CPU+NPU session forms remain adequate).
Stopped NPU command: a modeled 852-to-492 MHz retune after 70 seconds performs the existing five writes, 65 register reads and 11 validated clock reads in 236 modeled microseconds. Same-rate success performs no writes, seven register reads and five validated clock reads. The counts include ownership checks.
Cases: thirteen selected provider cases cover late lifetime, same-rate ownership, expired commands, busy locks and retained failure, including expiry during PLL completion. The actual OS mailbox fixture (checks/os-npu-perf-mailbox.c) covers queued/executing exclusion and matching answers. The final resident card producer passes 21 focused authority and admission cases. Six linked native cases cover resident admission and operation 8 after 70 seconds, including stale epochs and an occupied mailbox. The accepted GPU service, shared-engine and CPU/NPU owner checks supply the transition, exhausted-budget and thermal-interruption evidence; their reviewed sources are integrated unchanged. Cold monitor, card generation and stamping and recognition arithmetic evidence are reused without replay.
Reproduction of the mailbox check: from the repository root, use an existing configured NPU OS build (BUILD) for its FreeRTOS and application include paths; the host fixture includes the actual OS NPU source (apps/os/npu.c) and models only scheduler calls and the provider answer; compile checks/os-npu-perf-mailbox.c with clang using the include paths from that build's compile_commands.json row for apps/os/npu.c (excluding newlib), -std=c11 -O1 -g -Wall -Wextra -Werror -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections, the sanitizer flags of checks/harness.py, and the definitions SUNSTONE_BOARD_SUPERVISED=1, SUNSTONE_BOARD_RESIDENT=1, SUNSTONE_A733_OS_NPU=1, SUNSTONE_A733_OS_PERF=1 and OS_PERF_BOOT_MODE=1, then run the executable. The check does not build or run an inference image.
